lane: B3 — NEW FEATURE: radar / spider chart of a unit's stats on the character and tower sheets
owner_item: "In the character sheets and the tower sheets, we need to have a radar chart or spider chart… there's like five or six points… a level one character like a bat would have like 1,1,1,1 and then the speed and the attack speed… and then you look at the freaking Vlad and it would be mega developed [by] compare… it should probably be in that empty area just to the right of the stats — because it says attack, penetration, whatever, HP, defense, and then it gives the number, and then there's a bunch of empty space, and then all the way on the right it says the total pool of health and the total output of damage. So between those there should be a little graph."
root_cause: NOT A BUG — a new build. What is CONFIRMED is that the region the owner describes exists exactly as described and is measurable from the shipped layout constants. `characterSheet.draw` lays every stat row out in THREE columns and nothing else (`characterSheet.ts:415-417`): label at `x + PAD`, number at `x + PAD + valueCol`, `derived` RIGHT-ALIGNED at `x + w - PAD`. The gap between column 2 and column 3 is empty on every card, and on PEN/DEF rows the whole right half is empty because `statRowsFor` sets `derived: null` (`characterSheetModel.ts:606,608`). MEASURED free band: CREATURE card ~95.8 x 80 px at (x+55.6..x+151.4, y+134..y+214); TOWER card only ~48.6 x 100-120 px because `valueCol` jumps from 28 to 74 for the label CONNECTORS; CASTLE card ~106 x 80 px at PANEL_W 268. Vertical slack under the rows is only ~26 px (heightFor(4,false)=240, last row bottom y+214) — the space is HORIZONTAL, as he said.

evidence.why_it_matters: THE WHOLE LAYOUT, in three lines. Label left, number at a derived column, derived string right-aligned at the far edge. The owner's 'bunch of empty space' is the interval between line 2's end and line 3's start. Nothing else is drawn on a stat row, so the band is genuinely free.

With `const top = y + PAD + 36;` at :334, the stat block starts at y+12+36+76+10 = y+134 and advances by ROW_H 20. That fixes the band's top edge and its height exactly: 4 rows = 80 px for a creature, 5-6 rows for a tower.

The left edge of the band is derived from the WIDEST LABEL PRESENT, not a constant. 'ATK' gives 28; 'CONNECTORS' gives 74. That is why the tower card's band is half the creature card's, and why the radar must be sized from this function rather than from a literal. Re-deriving a constant here is the CONNECT4RS defect statColumn.test.ts was written for.

The measurement inputs. Note PAD/PORTRAIT/BAR_H/ROW_H are DUPLICATED at characterSheet.ts:50-53 — the renderer keeps its own copies. A radar must NOT add a third copy: the band rectangle belongs in the model (which already exports SHEET_W to the renderer) and the renderer consumes it.

FOUR OF THE AXES ALREADY EXIST AS RAW STATS, and the derived totals (pool, a-swing) are the things on the right the chart must NOT duplicate. This is the confirmation the brief asked for: the axes are the raw HP/DEF/ATK/PEN points, and they are already in hand at the call site — no new lookup, no second scale.

SPEED IS A REAL FIELD and it is this one. Its own docblock at :180 says 'The ONLY thing that drives locomotion is `maxAccel` (creatureVerlet.computeSteeringAccel reads `config.maxAccel` and nothing else)'. `hopSpeedMul` is the trap — S153 shipped a speed retune through it that could not do anything.
⛔ SPEED IS NOT INVERTED. The test's own ladder is 'STRICTLY DESCENDING' with hound/bat fastest at the top, and it measures maxAccel. Higher = faster. Normalise it directly, do not flip it.

evidence.quote: attackCadenceTicks: 300, // legacy span; the gnaw now runs until the connector gives way
evidence.why_it_matters: ⛔⛔ ATTACK SPEED IS THE ONE AXIS WITH LIARS IN THE TABLE. `attackCadenceTicks` IS inverted (ticks per cycle, lower = faster), but the pencil chewer's 300 is dead legacy — its real bite rate is CHEW_INTERVAL_TICKS 60 (constants.ts:1354, consumed by creatureLifecycle.ts:47). A naive axis draws the chewer as the slowest attacker in the game at 1/5 speed when it bites once a second like everyone else.

determinism_risk:
NONE-RENDER-ONLY. No PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (stays 47), no four-sites obligation, no new GameEffect, no wire field, no hash sub-site, no save-format change.

Verified rather than assumed, three ways:
1. `characterSheet.ts:15-20` — "THE SELECTION IS AN ID AND NEVER ENTERS `world` … that is what keeps this feature off the hash, out of the save format and off the wire". The card is already outside the sim by construction.
2. `Creature` carries NO stat fields (`src/state/creatures/creature.ts:409-445` is id / type / ownerPlayerId / pos / prevPos / targetPos / targetBondId / targetCreatureId). Every axis value is read from `CREATURE_CONFIGS` / `DEFENDER_CONFIGS`, static tables keyed by a type both peers already agree on. Two peers cannot disagree about a bat's ATK.
3. Nothing here is a per-strike visual, so the `world.effects` 10 Hz-sampled / 60 Hz-wiped hazard in protocol.ts does not apply — the chart is re-derived every frame from synced state, which is the pattern that rule asks for.

The one thing that is NOT free: `radarGeometry` uses `Math.cos` / `Math.sin`. That is fine here because it runs in the RENDERER only and never touches `world.tick`, but it must not be imported by anything under `src/state/`. Worth a one-line comment at the top of the new file saying so.
art_cost:
NO-ART. Entirely procedural Pixi `Graphics` — `poly().fill().stroke()` plus `moveTo/lineTo` spokes. Zero generation, zero atlas, zero asset bytes, no bundle-size movement worth measuring (bundle sits at 852.2 / 1000 KiB, 147.8 KiB headroom, measured S182).

The precedents are already in the tree and named: `codexPresentation.ts:300` `drawEmblem` (moveTo/lineTo + stroke, pure-layout / thin-draw split), `ui.ts:1187` `g.poly(pts).fill({ color: player.color, alpha: 0.9 })` (filled polygon), `avatarRenderer.ts:188`, `creatureRenderer.ts:715`. `ART_PIPELINE.md` is not engaged at all — nothing in this lane needs a clip, a seed still, or the 12-frame packer.

The colour is free too: the chart takes `v.accent`, the race colour the card already resolves at `characterSheet.ts:319-327` under R181.
tests_owed:
⚠ **NO RENDERER RUNS UNDER VITEST** — `vite.config.ts:72-101` sets no `environment`, so the suite runs in plain node with no DOM and no WebGL. Helga drew on top of her own hall with the whole suite green. Stating plainly what can and cannot be pinned:

**CAN BE PROPERLY PINNED (pure functions, `src/render/characterSheetRadar.test.ts`, NEW):**
· `radarGeometry` — n points for n axes; first axis at angle -PI/2 (straight up); a value of `max` lands exactly on radius r; a value of 0 lands at the floor, not at the centre; `value > max` clamps rather than escaping the band; every returned point is finite (no NaN from a 0 max or an empty axis list).
· THE OWNER'S OWN EXAMPLE AS A TEST: feed `t3Bat` (2/0/2/1) and `t9BossVampires` (20/8/10/10) through the real configs and assert Vlad's hull AREA is several times the bat's. That is his "mega developed" stated as an assertion instead of a screenshot.
· `rosterAxisMaxima` — asserts the maxima are DERIVED (poison one config, watch the max move) and that no shipped unit exceeds any axis, so a future retune cannot silently clip Vlad off the top. This is the same two-lane discipline `statsLadder.test.ts:95-106` already uses and should cite it.
· `radarBand` — ⛔ THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: assert the band never overlaps the value column NOR the right-aligned derived column, for BOTH label sets — `['ATK','PEN','HP','DEF']` (valueCol 28) and `['CONNECTORS','SHAPES','ATK','PEN','RANGE']` (valueCol 74) — and for the longest derived strings actually produced ("150 a swing", "462 pool", "not bought"). This is the CONNECT4RS regression class, and `statColumn.test.ts` is the precedent to mirror.
· Existing `src/render/characterSheetModel.test.ts` gains one case: a creature view carries a non-null `radar` of the agreed length; a tower carries whatever the ruling decides.

**CANNOT BE PINNED BY THE UNIT SUITE, and I will not pretend otherwise:** that the polygon actually REACHES the screen, that it lands inside the band on a live card, that it does not z-fight the stat text, that `this.g` is not leaking children. A source-text tripwire in `characterSheet.wired.test.ts` can assert the draw call EXISTS — ⛔ and per S182's rule it proves a line exists, NOT that it is reached. If it is added it must state that limit on itself, the way `characterSheet.wired.test.ts:19-21` already does.

**THE ONLY THING THAT WOULD ACTUALLY PROVE IT ON SCREEN** is a Playwright observation in `npm run e2e:gating` (65 tests / 17 files) that opens a card and screenshots it. Cheap-ish, but it is a new e2e file and `src/ci.e2eLanes.test.ts` pins the lane mapping — so if the branch adds one, that file joins the file_set and becomes a collision point with any other lane touching e2e. Recommend: ship without it, and have the owner eyeball one card, which is a 10-second check he is already doing every session.

· **If the owner has not answered the TOWER question**, ship the tower path OFF — `radar: null` for a structure card — and write the test that turns red when someone enables it without a ruling. A tower card then looks exactly as it does today; nothing regresses.

One caveat on the measurements in this report, stated honestly: the pixel band is computed from the shipped constants and `MONO_EM_RATIO` 0.6, which is the same estimate the card's own text fitting already uses (`characterSheetModel.ts:626-629`, `characterSheet.ts:90`). It is an ESTIMATE of glyph advance, not a rendered measurement — no renderer runs under vitest, so nothing in this repo measures real text width. The whole reason `radarBand` must be a derived function rather than a literal rectangle is that the same estimate then governs the radar and the text together, so they cannot drift apart.
